Subject: Pricing exhibit question — bundling & floor treatment

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — OrbitSoft is excited about Redwood for inference consolidation. I’m pulling together the procurement packet and have one clarification on the pricing schedules before we loop finance:

1) Exhibit B (pricing table) includes a product-level floor for each SKU and a separate order-level ‘stabilizer’ clause. Our procurement team reads the floor as preventing per-SKU credits from being applied below the listed floor (i.e., the floor is per-SKU, not aggregated). Can you confirm if that’s Redwood’s intent?

2) We do a lot of bundling across SKUs in practice (embedding + chat + rouge reranking). If we accept a bundled discount, is Redwood willing to allow smoothing across SKUs for the purpose of the floor (so a pack-level shortfall can be covered by overperformance in another SKU), or does the floor block cross-SKU smoothing entirely?

We want to avoid an outcome where the bundle discount pushes one SKU under its floor and triggers a true-up that retroactively changes credits across the whole contract. Any suggested wording or precedent examples would help.

I can share a quick sketch of our expected SKU mix for year 1 if that helps.

Regards,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Procurement, OrbitSoft

1) Marissa (cc’d) to comment on commercial playbook and propose a smoothing matrix we can offer.

Sanjay — quick commercial framing from our side: we can offer a ‘bundle smoothing allowance’ with these guardrails:

- Scope: smoothing applies only across the SKUs listed in Annex A (embedding, chat-gen, rerank).
- Cap: cumulative negative variance offset limited to 12% of the aggregate committed value per quarter.
- Waterfall: first use any per-SKU overperformance in the quarter, then apply from pack-level reserve.
- Review cadence: quarterly reconciliation with a 30-day cure window to avoid retroactive true-ups unless repeated across two consecutive quarters.

This keeps the Exhibit floor in place while preventing a single SKU drop from causing immediate retroactive adjustments. If OrbitSoft prefers a higher cap we can consider but would need a stepped price or commitment uplift.

Karthik / Laura — can you confirm whether the above is implementable within the orderform language (I can send a sample matrix).

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Commercial Ops, Redwood

Subject: Fwd: Pricing exhibit question — bundling & floor treatment (legal redline)

Marissa / Diego — forwarding a redline recommendation for Exhibit B and the Order Form annex. Key legal points (high level):

1) Maintain per-SKU floor language but add a defined “Pack Smoothing” section. Draft language should:
   - Define "Pack Smoothing" as a quarterly-only reconciliation mechanism;
   - Specify that smoothing may not reduce the effective per-SKU floor below 85% of the listed floor without an express amendment signed by both parties;
   - Include an audit right limited to sampling for reconciling credits.

2) True-ups: preserve a 30-day cure period and limit retroactive billing adjustments to instances where aggregate reconciliation over two consecutive quarters exceeds the 12% cap.

3) Data portability: if smoothing applies, require both parties to agree on the telemetry/metrics used for SKU performance (sequence length buckets, tokenized volumes, embedding vector counts). Call out that discrepancies resolved by Redwood’s consolidated reporting are binding for billing purposes unless material error (>5%).

I attached a marked-up PDF with inline edits and an OrderForm annex with the matrix Marissa suggested. I kept the commercial guardrails but added explicit thresholds to avoid open-ended cross-subsidies.
